title: Document AI pipeline: queue it, then chunk it
brief: Users upload documents; each one gets an LLM summary and goes into search. The file goes to blob storage. The LLM handles 5 calls/s per replica (about 2 s each, $3/hr). Uploads must stay fast and summaries must not pile up.

requirements: 20 uploads/s (writes), one LLM call per document
variants.twist: The LLM provider is down for 30 s: kill_node on the LLM block, then restore_node. Do uploads keep working? Watch the backlog build, get redelivered, and drain.

requirements: 10 uploads/s of long PDFs: each is split into 8 chunks that are summarized separately, then combined
Mark the worker's edge into the LLM as fan-out on write (the lesson sets followers = 8): one document becomes 8 calls
variants.twist: Customers start uploading 200-page contracts: 16 chunks per document. Apply with set_traffic(followers=16). Scale the GPUs, use bigger chunks (fewer calls, longer each), or summarize only what gets searched?

hints: Does the uploader need the summary before the upload returns?
Accept the upload, store it, and hand the summary to a queue; size the GPUs for the calls per second that come out of it. A document split into chunks is several calls, not one.

Bulk: the request only stores the file and enqueues; size the GPU pool from documents/s and add a little headroom. Long docs: the rate that reaches the GPUs is documents/s x chunks per document. Which edge has to fan out for the sim to see that?
_notes: Bulk: sync (service -> LLM) gives upload p99 ~2.5 s and timeout errors. Async: service -> blob + queue -> worker -> LLM. 5 replicas (rho 0.8): p99 ~95 ms, $15.50; 3 fall behind (backlog over 100 within 30 s); 9 ($27.50) break the budget. Long docs: 80 LLM calls/s. 17 replicas (rho 0.94): $51.50; 18: $54.50; 15 can't keep up; 20 ($60.50) break the budget. Sync with the same fan-out collapses (98% errors). Failed summaries are redelivered from the queue (at least once), so an LLM outage shows up as backlog and the queue's redelivery rate, not as lost work. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
